label: PF Backlog 549
title: Defect/RCCA: CI (py3.11) broken by f-strings with a backslash inside {...} (PEP 701 is 3.12+); add a pycompat guard
body:
## Problem / why
The `structure` CI job failed on EVERY develop push (~14s) at `import core` - before any gate ran.
CI runs Python 3.11; local dev runs 3.14, so the code was green locally but a SyntaxError in CI.

## 5-Why (RCCA)
1. CI died importing `core/__init__` -> SyntaxError in `core/presentation_generator.py:645`.
2. The f-string had `\n` inside a replacement field `{...}` (a nested f-string inside the braces).
3. Python 3.11 forbids a backslash in an f-string expression part; 3.12 (PEP 701) relaxed it.
4. Dev machine runs 3.14, so the construct parsed; nothing enforced the CI target interpreter (3.11).
5. No compatibility guard + no pinned interpreter -> 3.12-only syntax can ship.
ROOT CAUSE: dev/CI interpreter divergence (3.14 vs 3.11) with no guard.
Same class found in 3 places: presentation_generator.py:645, code_executor.py:146, customer_onboarding.py:115.

## Corrective
Hoist the backslash out of the replacement field in all 3 sites (build the string in a local var / use chr(10)).

## Guard (new - prevents recurrence)
`scripts/dev/pycompat_check.py`: flags a backslash inside an f-string replacement field (any nesting).
Wired into the fast `precheck` tier AND the pre-commit hook (changed .py files).

## Acceptance criteria (G/W/T)
- Given a file with a backslash inside an f-string `{...}`, when `pycompat_check` runs, then it exits 1.
- Given the clean tree, then `precheck` fast/`--full` is green and the CI `structure` job passes.
- Given a dev on 3.12+, then the guard still catches the 3.11-incompatible construct.

## Verification / test plan
`python scripts/dev/pycompat_check.py` (whole tree) + `python scripts/dev/precheck.py` fast tier.
